title: PRD revision: define verifiable runtime-degradation contracts and acceptance tests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
After the Q1 coldstart/autoscale incident, the postmortem produced runnable action items but our PRD lacks precise, testable acceptance criteria and rollout gates for runtime degradation behavior. This ticket updates the Serving Runtime PRD to (1) codify degradation contracts (latency, error-rate, fallback rules), (2) add synthetic and regression acceptance tests, and (3) link runbook triggers to PRD gates so deploys are automatically validated.

Goal:
Deliver an updated PRD section that translates incident learnings into verifiable product requirements developers and SREs can use to implement and validate fallbacks and rollback criteria. The PRD should minimize ambiguity so engineering, QA, and on-call have a shared pass/fail definition for new serving releases.
postmortem_summary: Incident: 2025-01-28 coldstart/autoscale under-provisioning. Key failures: delayed warm pool ramp, KV cache misses at high fanout, and inconsistent fallback to smaller model variants that caused client-visible latency spikes. Postmortem recommended: explicit degradation thresholds, synthetic verification for warm-pool and fallback logic, and automated rollback triggers tied to SLO deviation. See: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/postmortem-coldstart-2025-01-28
proposed_changes:
1) Add a 'Degradation Contracts' subsection with numeric thresholds: 95th-percentile tail latency < 350ms for 'warm' traffic profile, P90 latency < 220ms, client-visible error-rate < 0.1%. Define 'graceful fallback' semantics: fallback must be a model variant with compatible output shape and documented score deltas.
2) Define synthetic acceptance tests: warm-pool scaling test, KV cache warmup test (traffic replay + expected hit-rate > 60% after 3s), fallback correctness regression (end-to-end test verifying output structure and example prompt quality thresholds).
3) Add automated rollout gates: Canary for 2% traffic with 10-minute synthetic verification window; block rollout if synthetic tests fail or if service-level alert fires.
4) Update rollback criteria: sustained SLO breach (P90 latency > 300ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows) or increase in client error-rate > 0.5% absolute.
5) Link these into the Deploy Runbook and Console dashboard checks (add synthetic check panel and traffic-graded canary view).
scope: In scope: PRD text changes, formalized acceptance criteria, synthetic test definitions, runbook links, dashboard panel mockups, and CI job definitions (test harness integration). Out of scope: implementing runtime changes, model retraining, or infra scaling automation — those are separate ENG tickets that will reference this PRD.
acceptance_criteria:
- PRD updated in Confluence with 'Degradation Contracts' and 'Synthetic Acceptance Tests' sections.
- Each numeric threshold has owner and measurement method documented.
- Synthetic test manifests (kitchen-sink JSON or CI job scripts) are checked into the 'runtime-e2e' repo and referenced in the PRD.
- Console dashboard mockups attached and linked to a dashboard ticket.
- Rollout gate definitions include canary %, duration, and explicit pass/fail criteria.
- SRE and two runtime engineers have signed off on the wording (Slack thread + approval comment).
- QA has an integration plan to run synthetic tests during pre-release canaries.
- Document lists follow-up ENG tickets for automation work with owners assigned.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft PRD update and circulate to SRE + runtime-eng for review (1 week). 2) Finalize acceptance tests and add synthetic CI jobs (parallel with ENG planning). 3) Attach dashboard mocks and submit console-ticket for panel implementation. 4) Blocker review and sign-off in weekly release sync; merge PRD. 5) Track ENG implementation tickets (autoscale fixes, cache warmup, fallback plumbing) and verify CI tests land before release to canary.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overly strict thresholds could block releases unnecessarily. Mitigation: Use staged thresholds (strict for canary verification, lenient for initial rollout) and add an emergency-override process documented in PRD.
Risk: Synthetic tests create maintenance burden. Mitigation: Keep tests scoped, reuse traffic-replay harness, allocate one eng rotation to maintain tests.
Risk: Ambiguity in 'compatible output' for fallback models. Mitigation: Add a compatibility checklist and require explicit model-variant contracts in model-onboarding PRD section.
